content: The effect or concentration of atazanavir can be influenced by its interaction with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. 1. Atazanavir and Ritonavir/Cobicistat-containing HIV Regimens: Patients on these regimens should continue their treatment as prescribed. Monitor for increased adverse effects related to nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or other protease inhibitors when used concurrently. 2. Atazanavir and Nisoldipine: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Atazanavir and Norethindrone/Norethindrone Acetate/Norgestimate/Norgestrel: Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of these agents by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternatives should be considered if available. 4. Atazanavir and Oliceridine: Atazanavir increases the levels of oliceridine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. 5. Atazanavir and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir & Dasabuvir (DSC): Atazanavir increases the levels of paritaprevir when co-administered. Adjust atazanavir dosing to 300 mg (without ritonavir) in the morning when used with Viekira Pak. 6. Atazanavir and Ondansetron: Atazanavir increases ondansetron levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dosage adjustment is recommended, but caution is advised. 7. Atazanavir and Orlistat: Orlistat decreases atazanavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction may lead to loss of virological control in HIV-infected patients. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 8. Atazanavir and Osilodrostat: Atazanavir increases osilodrostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Atazanavir and Panobinostat: Atazanavir increases panobinostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Atazanavir and Paricalcitol: Atazanavir increases paricalcitol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 11. Atazanavir and Beta Blockers (Penbutolol, Pindolol, Timolol): Atazanavir enhances the effects of these beta blockers through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta blocker dose. 12. Atazanavir and Perampanel: Atazanavir increases perampanel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Atazanavir and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Atazanavir increases the levels of unconjugated MMAE (a CYP3A4 substrate) from polatuzumab vedotin, potentially increasing toxicity. Monitor closely. 14. Atazanavir and Pramlintide: Atazanavir may decrease the effects of pramlintide due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 15. Atazanavir and Prednisolone/Prednisone: Atazanavir increases the levels of these corticosteroids by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Atazanavir and Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel, Micronized, Natural): Atazanavir increases progesterone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Atazanavir and Protriptyline/Trimipramine: Atazanavir increases the levels of these tricyclic antidepressants through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Atazanavir and Quinine/Quinidine: Atazanavir increases the levels of these agents by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Atazanavir and Repaglinide: Atazanavir increases repaglinide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Atazanavir and Rivaroxaban: Atazanavir increases rivaroxaban levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Atazanavir and Rosuvastatin: Atazanavir increases rosuvastatin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Use alternatives if available and monitor closely. 22. Atazanavir and Salmeterol: Atazanavir increases salmeterol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of systemic toxicity. Use alternatives if available and monitor closely. 23. Atazanavir and Saxagliptin: Atazanavir increases saxagliptin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust saxagliptin dosage to 2.5 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Atazanavir and Sitagliptin: Atazanavir may decrease sitagliptin effects due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 25. Atazanavir and Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate: This agent decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer atazanavir at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 26. Atazanavir and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Atazanavir increases the levels of these agents by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Atazanavir and Tadalafil: Atazanavir increases tadalafil levels by decreasing its metabolism. Stop tadalafil 24 hours before initiating atazanavir and restart at a reduced dose after 7 days. 28. Atazanavir and Warfarin: Atazanavir may increase warfarin's less potent R-enantiomer by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust warfarin dose as needed. 29. Atazanavir and Zidovudine: Both agents increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 30. Atazanavir and Zileuton: Atazanavir increases zileuton levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 31. Atazanavir and Zuranolone: Atazanavir increases zuranolone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zuranolone dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Atazanavir and Minor Interactions: Atazanavir may interact with various agents (e.g., aliskiren, ambrisentan, amlodipine, clarithromycin, dapsone, darunavir, dexamethasone, etc.) through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown, but caution is advised. These interactions highlight the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when atazanavir is co-administered with other medications.
